expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the headline and the first sentence of each finding block's What field tells the author what is wrong and how bad it is; no first sentence is a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: Headline: 'Hold. The branch breaks three project invariants and lets a discount code produce a negative charge.' Titles state the defect (e.g. 'C3: Migration 002 drops the plan field in one step and has no down()'). Weakest first sentences are context-only (H2 'This endpoint is new, and the description does not mention it.'; M1 'These changes ride along...') but the headline carries the defect. No qualifier chains.

notes: Strongest verification of the old-skill arm: an independent defect-first agent plus a separate verifier tried to refute 8 candidates and refuted one sub-claim (import cycle), which the report records as REFUTED. Severity: email normalization rated Critical, tests rated High; both defensible. S4 surfaced only as a Known limitation and dismissed for the in-memory store. S9: every run names the call-site '-' strip as a bypass of parse_money's non-negative guard, but none says the fix 'belongs in util.parse_money'. All instead cite the parse_money docstring ('adjustments are modeled explicitly') and propose an explicit credit model. I graded S9 on the named mechanism (call-site special case working around the helper) and passed it uniformly. The assertion's remedy clause conflicts with the fixture's own docstring and should be reworded, e.g. 'flags the call-site negative special case as a band-aid around util.parse_money's contract'. S4: no run in the iteration rated the check-then-act race as a PLAUSIBLE Issue as the README expects. Runs that mention it put it in Known limitations or a Fix clause, so a pass means the mechanism is named, not that it is calibrated. S5 passes at Low or Suggestion severity; the assertion does not demand a severity. The skim test is subjective: graded on finding headlines plus the first What sentence, since every headline states the defect and the section gives the severity.
